introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2025. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub mark in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH paper are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

Calculators are Allowed.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

La mention « only the first four questions answered will be marked » est recopiee dans `introduction_markdown`.

Aucun corrige officiel : les corriges sont des reponses modeles redigees sans source consultable. Les faits cites (lieux, institutions, exemples) sont des faits reconnus ; aucune statistique precise n'est avancee. Contenu a faire relire par un geographe avant toute mise en avant.

Fautes d'impression du sujet conservees dans les enonces : « George » (gorge), « hallow » (hollow), « chanel » (channel), « Floodpalin » (floodplain), « under development », « TWO importance », « Briefly describe 1HREE ». Elles sont lues comme les termes usuels dans les corriges.

Question 7(a) : les bassins et les cours d'eau cites sont ceux d'usage courant dans les manuels (Atlantique : Sanaga, Wouri, Nyong, Ntem, Mungo ; Niger : Benoue, Faro ; Congo : Dja, Boumba, Ngoko ; Tchad : Logone). L'attribution des cours d'eau secondaires est a faire relire.

Question 7(d) : realisations et strategies citees de memoire (Vision 2035, DSCE, SND30, port de Kribi, barrages de Lom Pangar et de Memve'ele, autoroute Douala-Yaounde) ; aucune date ni statistique precise n'est avancee. Les chantiers « en cours » evoluent : a faire relire avant mise en avant.

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) Name:

(i) **TWO** drainage basins and **TWO** rivers of each of the basins.
(ii) One physical and one human touristic potential.

(4+2=6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two drainage basins and two rivers of each (4 marks).**

| Drainage basin | Two rivers |
|---|---|
| **Atlantic (Gulf of Guinea) basin** | The Sanaga and the Wouri (also the Nyong, the Ntem and the Mungo) |
| **Niger basin (River Benue)** | The Benue and the Faro |

(Other correct basins: the **Congo basin**, with the Dja, the Boumba and the Ngoko, which flow into the Sangha; and the **Lake Chad basin**, with the Logone and its tributaries.)

**(ii) One physical and one human tourist potential (2 marks, one mark each).**

- **Physical:** Mount Cameroon (the highest mountain of West and Central Africa) at Buea; or the beaches and the Lobe Falls at Kribi; or the Waza National Park (wildlife) in the Far North.
- **Human (cultural):** the royal palaces of the Fon of Bafut or of the Sultan of Foumban (with its museum), or the lamidates of the north, or traditional festivals, dances and handicrafts.

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) Describe **THREE** problems hindering industrial development in Cameroon.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three problems (2 marks each: the problem and its description):

1. **Inadequate and unreliable energy supply.** Power cuts and high costs of electricity raise the cost of production, make machines stop and discourage investors.
2. **Poor transport and other infrastructure.** Many roads are in bad condition, the railway network is small and the ports are congested, so raw materials and finished goods are delayed and cost more, particularly between the regions and the hinterland.
3. **Shortage of capital and skills, and a small market.** Banks lend at high interest rates to small businesses, there are too few trained technicians and managers, the low purchasing power of the people limits local sales, and local products face competition from cheaper imported and smuggled goods.

(Other accepted problems: high taxes and bureaucracy, corruption, and the dependence on imported machines and spare parts.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Explain **TWO** measures aimed at conserving fish resources.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two measures (2 marks each: the measure and its explanation):

1. **Regulating the methods of fishing.** The law fixes the minimum size of the mesh of the nets and bans harmful methods (such as the use of poison or explosives), so that young fish can escape and grow and breed; licences and quotas limit the number of boats and the catch.
2. **Closed seasons and protected areas.** Fishing is forbidden at certain times (the breeding season) or in some places (protected breeding grounds), so that fish stocks recover; patrols check illegal fishing, and pollution of rivers and the sea is controlled.

(Another measure: fish farming (aquaculture) in ponds relieves the pressure on natural fish stocks.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
d) State **FOUR** efforts being made by the government to emerge by 2035.

(4 marks)

Total (20 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon's "Vision 2035" aims to make the country an emerging country, and efforts being made by the government include (any four, one mark each):

1. **Building infrastructure:** roads and motorways (such as the Douala-Yaounde motorway), bridges, the Kribi deep-sea port and other ports.
2. **Increasing the production of electricity:** dams such as Lom Pangar and Memve'ele and other hydroelectric projects.
3. **Modernising agriculture and encouraging agro-industries** (the "second generation agriculture").
4. **Promoting industrialisation and the processing of raw materials locally,** and encouraging private and foreign investment.
5. **Improving education and professional training,** and health services, to have a skilled and healthy workforce.
6. **Planning strategies:** the Growth and Employment Strategy Paper and the National Development Strategy 2020-2030 (NDS30) that implement the vision.
